paragraphs.source_en: On December seventeenth, Hidetada returned from the capital. Tokugawa Ieyasu had learned from another source that Hideyoshi intended to enter Nagoya Castle on the first day of the third month the following spring. For Hideyoshi, the first day of the third month was highly auspicious. His conquest of Kyushu had begun on the first day of the third month in Tenshō fifteen, and the Odawara campaign on the first day of the third month in Tenshō eighteen. This time, he surely meant to surpass both former victories and achieve an overwhelming triumph.

paragraphs.source_en: Yet the scale of Hideyoshi’s expedition was far greater than Ieyasu had imagined. The main army was divided into sixteen contingents. With the ships’ crews, the first and second auxiliary contingents, and Hideyoshi’s hatamoto corps added, the force for the coming spring exceeded 281,800 men. If servants and laborers other than the soldiers were also counted, the total would approach one million.
